newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FOCUS-Ireland's AIB has record H1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Ireland's AIB has record H1 earnings.

text.p: Allied Irish Banks Plc on Thursday reported record growth in earnings in the first half of 1997, with all divisions contributing to a strong performance.

The bank said pre-tax profit for the six months ended June 30, 1997 rose by 20 percent to 242.2 million Irish pounds ($354.3 million), well above analysts' expectations which ranged from 228 to 232 million.
Earnings per share rose by 22 percent to 22.3 Irish pence while AIB's return on equity increased to 22.3 percent, the highest in the bank's history.
"In the last six months we have seen a quantum leap in the business of the group," chief executive Tom Mulcahy said.

"This impressive half-year performance comes at a time when AIB has just completed two landmark transactions - the acquisition of Dauphin Deposit Corporation in the U.S. and the majority investment in WBK in Poland."
AIB said in a statement that good demand for its products and services in the Republic of Ireland, Northern Ireland and Britain was one of the key factors behind the increase.

The bank also attributed the rise in profits to growth in retail and commercial lending in the U.S. and a large rise in fee income and to a substantially increased contribution from its capital markets division, particularly Treasury operations.
AIB's U.S. operations reported an 11 percent rise in profits to 62.9 million Irish pounds while profits in the capital markets division rose by 33 percent to 42.6 million.
AIB's new Polish subsidiary Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK), in which it holds a 60 percent stake, made a profit contribution of 12.3 million Irish pounds after funding.
The bank was silent on whether it had any plans to exercise its option to buy back up to 50 million of its own shares.

AIB has shareholder approval to buy back the shares from the U.S. shareholders of Dauphin Deposit Corp DAPN.O who opted for shares rather than cash in AIB's recent $1.36 billion acquisition of the U.S. bank.
AIB's share price rose 28 Irish pence to 623 by 0900 GMT. ($ = 0.683 Irish Pounds)
